To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HBcAg capsid protein can be assembled into two types of icosahedral capsid, and the T = 3 icosahedral particle has been crystallized.
we have crystallized T = 3, and T = 3 icosahedral capsid particles, which are composed of 90 and of 120 dimers of HBcAg, respectively.

(1) the HBcAg capsid can be crystallized in two different icosahedral forms, T = 3 (diameter = 27 nm) and T = 2 (diameter = -35 nm), which are composed of 90 and120 dimers, (2) HBcAg dimers can be crystallized as a separate entity, (3) HBcAg capsids can be crystallized with or without a DNA oligomer bound to their internal surface
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural characterization of the hepatitis B core protein and the capsid of the hepatitis B viral nucleocapsid, which is a homopolymeric assembly of 240 copies of the core protein.
the structural and functional analysis of the hepatitis B capsid protein.
the separation, crystallization, and preliminary X-ray analysis of two forms of hepatitis B virus capsid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T = 3 icosahedral capsids have been crystallized, and the crystals diffract to 8 A resolution.
the T = 3 particle is the native capsid of HBcAg, and the T = 4 particle is a mutant form of the capsid protein.
the capsid protein is a dimer, and that the T = 3 particle is a dimer of dimers and the T = 4 particle is a trimer of dimers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T = 3 icosahedral capsids were crystallized in the P3(1)21 space group (unit cell dimensions a = 150 A, b = 151 A, c = 170 A, alpha = 90 degrees, beta = 90 degrees and gamma = 120 degrees).
we were able to separate and crystallize two types of icosahedral capsids, each with a different number of dimers, from a mixture obtained from an E. coli expression system.
the T = 4 particle has a 4.5 A resolution electron density map and that the T =3 particle has a 3.5 A map.
The main takeaway from our work is that
T = 4 and T = 3 particles can be crystallized and that they are not identical.
the T = 4 particle is more stable than the T = 3 particle.
the HBc capsid protein is capable of forming both the T = 3 or T = 4 quaternary structure depending on the conditions under which it is assembled.
